findings.message: The admin CLI now gets the audit key through core's loadEnv (a class fix for that CLI). dev-seed's CLI entry still reads the key straight from the environment with `process.env.AUDIT_HASH_KEY!`. That skips the `min(32)` schema in packages/core/src/env.ts:15. An unset key also gets through as `undefined`, and `seedDevDemo` hands it to `configureRuntime`. Fix: read the key with `loadEnv().AUDIT_HASH_KEY` and stop when it is missing, as admin.ts now does. This entry is dev-only, so it can wait.
findings.scenario: AUDIT_HASH_KEY=short-key in .env.local, then run dev-seed → it signs the fixture audit rows with a 9-character key that the app refuses at boot. With no key set, the seed fails deep inside with the configureRuntime error instead of a clear message.

findings.message: Instance fix. Only the admin CLI now validates the audit key through core's loadEnv. The key rule still isn't enforced where the key is accepted: `configureRuntime` (packages/core/src/service.ts:38) and `setChainKey` (packages/core/src/chain-key.ts:15) take any non-empty string. Two other entry points that write to the audit chain still read the raw environment and skip the `min(32)` rule. (1) modules/delivery/sync/bin.ts:19-34 checks only that AUDIT_HASH_KEY is set, then calls `configureRuntime({ db, auditKey: env.AUDIT_HASH_KEY! })`. This is the production specclaw sync, and it writes audited proposal rows. (2) apps/web/scripts/dev-seed.ts:24/48 checks only that the key is truthy before it seeds audited fixtures. That makes the rule a second, looser copy again (B4). Fix the class: enforce the key rule once, in `configureRuntime`/`setChainKey`. Reuse core's env schema for AUDIT_HASH_KEY (export it) so the rule isn't written a third time, and throw on a key the app would refuse. Alternatively, route sync/bin.ts and dev-seed.ts through loadEnv() as well. Then add rows to a table-driven test for sync/bin.ts with an unset key, an empty key and a short key, each asserting a non-zero exit and no audit rows.
findings.scenario: Run `sync:specclaw` with AUDIT_HASH_KEY=short-key: it passes the set check, configureRuntime accepts the key, and syncSpecclaw writes proposal audit rows hashed with 'short-key'. The app refuses that key at boot, and with the deployment's real key verifyAuditChain fails on those rows. Running dev-seed with AUDIT_HASH_KEY=abc in .env.local has the same effect: the local chain is seeded with a key the app won't start with.
